Repo: `/Users/kostiantyn.vlasenko/Projects/leadv2` (the plugin repo — the single source; never create

reports a guarantee it does not actually deliver. None is a live incident today; each becomes one the
moment the surrounding condition changes.

Never run `git reset --hard`, `git clean` or `git stash` — shared trees. Do not move any branch
backwards past an existing commit.

## Item 1 (highest value) — router_v2 bypasses the arm ladder entirely

Founder order, executed as `3398d11` and re-executed today as `0445ca0` after a merge silently undid
it: **kimi is retired as a build/dispatch arm.** Today's fix expresses that as `dispatch: false` in
`plugins/leadv2/config/leadv2-routing.yaml`, enforced by `_load_dispatch_ladder` /
`_filter_ladder_to_dispatchable` in `plugins/leadv2/scripts/leadv2-dispatch-code.sh`, with a drift

resolver lists a retired arm, it can still be selected. It is inert today only because
`LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=0` — nothing guards it, so it ships silently the moment router_v2 is enabled.

- route v2's arm selection through the same dispatchable filter (not a second hand-kept exclusion
  list — the standing rule is *never hardcode an arm out of routing*; the retirement must remain
  expressed as config that both paths honour);

- a test that, with `LEADV2_ROUTER_V2=1`, a retired arm cannot be selected. It must FAIL against
  current HEAD.

reaching a real `kimi-coder.sh` / `glm-coder.sh` / `codex` invocation and prove it cannot; use the
existing poison-fence / `LEADV2_DISPATCH_SPAWN=0` / `LEADV2_DISPATCH_*_BIN` machinery.

inside persona-engine it finds that repo's own `.claude/ref/leadv2-routing.yaml` and fails to prove
degraded mode at all. Same commit, same code, opposite verdict depending on where you stood.

Fix: pin `PROJECT_ROOT="${TMP_ROOT}/degraded-root"` explicitly — the pattern every other test in the
file already uses via `CLAUDE_PROJECT_ROOT`. Then demonstrate the test gives the same result run from
at least three different cwds, one of which is inside a repo that HAS a routing config.

While you are there: sweep the rest of that file for the same cwd dependence and report what you
find, fixing any other instance.

## Item 3 — a resume test asserts "not 5" instead of "0"

`plugins/leadv2/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-resume-sentinel.sh:145-170` (S7) asserts `rc != 5` rather
than `rc == 0`. Exit 5 covers six distinct refusal reasons in `leadv2-dispatch-code.sh`, so a future
unrelated crash exiting with any other nonzero code would false-PASS. The observed rc really was 0,
so behaviour is right today; the assertion is just weaker than what was observed.

on my authority). Do not fix C2 in this lane — just make it visible and say whether it deserves its
own task.
